key_insight: Instead of retrieving external context at every reasoning step, an agentic controller can decide when to 'retrieve' vs when to 'think' (use internal reasoning), reducing noise and cost while improving downstream performance.
problem_solved: Retrieval-augmented pipelines indiscriminately perform retrieval at every step, incurring unnecessary compute and introducing irrelevant context that can hurt reasoning accuracy.
method: Introduce Agentic Context Evolution (ACE): an agentic controller that dynamically decides whether to trigger retrieval or rely on internal generation at each step.
Evolve the working context iteratively — selectively augmenting it only when utility signals (e.g., uncertainty, information gap, or expected value of retrieval) indicate benefit.
Maintain a compact, high-signal context by avoiding redundant retrievals and by updating context through targeted external lookups and internal synthesis.
impact: ACE lowers computational cost and context noise, yielding more efficient and often more accurate knowledge-intensive reasoning—beneficial for deploying large-scale LLM systems and building robust retrieval-augmented agents.
visual_elements: Side-by-side flowchart: brute-force retrieval-at-every-step vs ACE’s decision loop (agent decides retrieve vs think).
Bar chart: compute cost and accuracy comparison (always-retrieve vs ACE).
Schematic of context evolution: compact context maintained over iterations with occasional retrieval spikes.
Icon set: magnifying glass (retrieve), lightbulb (think), gauge (uncertainty signal), stopwatch (compute savings).
paper_title: To Retrieve or To Think? An Agentic Approach for Context Evolution
paper_authors: Rubing Chen, Jian Wang, Wenjie Li, Xiao-Yong Wei, Qing Li
